title: Fibrewise nonvanishing criterion for a multiplicative function norm
statement:
Let $p:Y	o Z$ be a finite morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. For all open $V\subseteq Z$ let $
u_V:\Gamma(p^{-1}V,\mathcal O_Y)	o\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_Z)$ preserve multiplication and $1$ and commute with restriction. Assume $b(y)=0$ implies $
u_V(b)(p(y))=0$ for every such $V,b$ and $y\in p^{-1}V$, with values in the residue fields [def-weil-residue-field]. For $b\in\Gamma(p^{-1}V,\mathcal O_Y)$ put $D(b)=\{y\in p^{-1}V:b(y)
e0\}$. Then for every $z\in V$ one has $$
u_V(b)(z)
e0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad p^{-1}(\{z\})\subseteq D(b).$$ Moreover, whenever the right side holds, $W=V\setminus p(p^{-1}V\setminus D(b))$ is an open neighborhood of $z$ in $Z$, $p^{-1}W\subseteq D(b)$, and there is $c\in\Gamma(p^{-1}W,\mathcal O_Y)$ such that $b|_{p^{-1}W}c=1$ and $
u_W(b|_{p^{-1}W})
u_W(c)=1$. No flatness, surjectivity, or power identity for $
u$ is assumed.

proof.text:
Fix $V,b$ and $z\in V$. If $
u_V(b)(z)
e0$ and $p(y)=z$, then $b(y)=0$ would give $
u_V(b)(z)=0$ by the assumed vanishing implication. Thus every such $y$ belongs to $D(b)$.

source.place: Section 0BCX (section-norms), neighborhood-unit observation; Tag 0BCZ (lemma-norm-map-invertible), final equivalence.

proof.text: Conversely assume $p^{-1}(\{z\})\subseteq D(b)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-function], $D(b)$ is open, so $C=p^{-1}V\setminus D(b)$ is closed in $p^{-1}V$. Choose a closed subset $F\subseteq Y$ with $C=F\cap p^{-1}V$, as allowed by the subspace topology. The finite morphism $p$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres]. Since $p(C)=p(F)\cap V$, the specified set $W=V\setminus p(C)=V\setminus p(F)$ is open in $Z$. The fibre assumption gives $z\notin p(C)$, hence $z\in W$. If $y\in p^{-1}W$ then $y\notin C$, so $p^{-1}W\subseteq D(b)$.

proof.text: By clause (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-function], there is an inverse $a$ to $b|_{D(b)}$. Restrict $a$ to the open $p^{-1}W\subseteq D(b)$ and call the resulting section $c$. Restrictions preserve products and $1$, so $b|_{p^{-1}W}c=1$.

source.place: Tag 01HZ (lemma-f-open), statement that the restriction to D(f) has an inverse; applied to the open subspace p^{-1}V.

proof.text:
Put $b_W=b|_{p^{-1}W}$. Multiplicativity and preservation of $1$ give $
u_W(b_W)
u_W(c)=
u_W(b_Wc)=
u_W(1)=1$. Evaluating in $\kappa(z)$ gives a product equal to $1$, so $
u_W(b_W)(z)
e0$. Restriction compatibility identifies this value with $
u_V(b)(z)$. This proves the converse and both asserted inverse identities.

Step 1 is the contrapositive of the vanishing hypothesis. Step 2 handles C being closed only in p^{-1}V correctly: it writes C = F ∩ p^{-1}V with F closed in Y, so p(C) = p(F) ∩ V and W = V \ p(F) is open. It cites lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-function (b) and lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres (1); both are Mathlib leaves, so they are tools and no tool_uses entry is needed. Step 3 uses clause (c) of the basic-open leaf and restricts the inverse to p^{-1}W. Step 4 multiplies, evaluates the unit in κ(z) and uses restriction compatibility; it is elementary. Edge cases checked: an empty fibre with p^{-1}W empty (zero ring, ν(1) = 1, consistent), the identity map, disjoint sheets with the product norm, and nonreduced Y. The parent lem-sfb-finite-norm-invertible-sections cites only the iff, under stronger hypotheses, so the citation is valid. A grep for 0BCX/0BCY/0BCZ and a reading of six norm-related nodes found no duplicate. All three search kinds are recorded, with the unavailable LeanSearch marked honestly. No SGA source is used.
